clue.text: Vault from feline over a rake

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so the cat comes first

parts.note: a feline is a cat
to rake is to comb, as through hair or soil

explanation.surface: A cat jumps from a vault, landing on a garden rake.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial chamber, and a vault is the same kind of tomb.

clue.text: Reportedly complete mess

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word for complete is given by its sound

parts.note: complete means whole

explanation.surface: A rumour that everything is a total shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a hole is to be in a mess or a predicament, a common idiom.

clue.text: Former sailor found in hold?

definitions.meaning: Horatio ..., the admiral killed at Trafalgar
a wrestling hold in which the arms lock the opponent's neck

explanation.surface: A retired seaman discovered down in a ship's cargo hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Nelson is Britain's most famous naval commander, and the full nelson is a standard wrestling grip.

clue.text: Underground place maybe giving topless humiliation

indicators.note: topless means the word for humiliation loses its first letter

parts.note: abasement is humiliation or degradation

explanation.surface: A seedy underground venue whose topless shows cause humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the A from the front of ABASEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is a storey below ground level, one example of an underground place, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Nuisance hurt hospital department holding idiot

indicators.note: holding means the first pieces wrap around the word for idiot

parts.note: to hurt is to harm
an ass is a fool
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A patient complains that a hospital unit with a fool in charge did them harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' wraps the two outer pieces around the idiot as one unit, so the insertion lands inside the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassment is persistent pestering, a nuisance inflicted on someone.

clue.text: Animal playing, catching tail of game bird

indicators.note: catching means the first pieces close around the letter taken from game

parts.note: a pig is an animal
a performance that is playing is on

indicators.note: tail of means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An animal at play catches the end of a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game bird' looks like one phrase, but 'bird' alone is the definition; 'catching' wraps both outer pieces round the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon is a common bird, so the general word covers this example.

clue.text: Lady in pub's imbibing singles …

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the pub's word takes the singles inside

parts.note: a bar is a pub; with the possessive it gives BARS
singles are ones

explanation.surface: A lady sits in the pub, drinking single measures.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis only joins this clue's surface to the next; 'imbibing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a noblewoman, formally addressed as Lady.

clue.text: Cautious swallows along with drink

indicators.note: swallows means the word for cautious takes another word inside it

parts.note: shy means wary or cautious
and means along with

explanation.surface: A careful drinker gulps a drink down with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink; 'swallows' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a long drink, so the general word stands for this example.

clue.text: … slowly, a short drink, in trouble

indicators.note: in means the a and short drink go inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: short means the word for drink loses its last letter

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Continuing the lady in the pub: she drinks slowly, a quick measure, and then gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis links the surface to the previous clue; 'short' trims the drink and 'in' places the result inside trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction meaning at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Appeared oddly clammier

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in the odd positions of clammier

explanation.surface: Someone showed up strangely sweatier than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Came, like appeared, means arrived or turned up.

clue.text: Red imitation of drink French rejected

parts.note: a sham is a fake or imitation

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the French phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: in French, 'of coffee' is de café, written DE CAFE

explanation.surface: A wine lover blushes at fake booze, which the French refuse to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DE CAFE (French for 'of coffee') into EFACED.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced people are embarrassed, and red is a way of saying flushed with embarrassment.

clue.text: Court sweetheart in empty declaration, emotionless

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: in puts the letter from sweet inside the emptied declaration
empty means only the outer letters of declaration remain

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E, a familiar crossword trick

explanation.surface: A suitor courts his sweetheart with a hollow, unfeeling declaration of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is not a lover here but the heart of 'sweet'; 'empty' leaves only the outside letters of declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden performance is stiff and expressionless, so the word means showing no feeling.

clue.text: Dogged, check this compiler's crossword, finally

parts.note: to check is to hold back or deter
the setter's own is mine

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of crossword

explanation.surface: A solver doggedly checks the setter's crossword to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged and determined both describe persistence that refuses to give up.

clue.text: Clothing curvy character wearing damsel's first girdle

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of damsel's
wearing means the curvy character has the following pieces around it

parts.note: a girdle is a ring encircling something
the letter S, spelt out as ess, is a curving character

explanation.surface: A damsel puts on a girdle that shows off her curvy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'curvy character' is the letter S, spelt out in full; 'wearing' puts it inside the damsel's initial and the girdle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing is the act of putting on clothes, so it means clothing in the sense of getting dressed.

clue.text: Happen to live facing sea

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
the tide is the sea's rise and fall, so it stands for the sea

explanation.surface: Someone happens to live with a view of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Betide means befall, as in 'woe betide you', so it means happen to someone.

clue.text: Dingy colour almost masking a fabric

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown, a dingy shade

indicators.note: masking means the shortened colour hides the a inside it
almost means the colour word loses its last letter

parts.note: green is a colour

explanation.surface: A drab-coloured fabric that almost hides its own shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GREEN to GREE; 'masking' puts A inside that, giving GAREE. 'Dingy colour' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungaree is a coarse cotton cloth, the fabric that gave dungarees their name.

clue.text: Spreads top of short pants

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of short

parts.note: trews are trousers; pants is the British word for trousers too

explanation.surface: Someone spreads the top of a pair of short trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: TREWS are close-fitting tartan trousers worn in Scotland. 'short pants' reads as one garment but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to scatter or spread things over a surface.

clue.text: Pure clothed in chaster lingerie

indicators.note: clothed in means the answer lies dressed inside these words

explanation.surface: Something pure is wrapped up in more modest underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling describes silver of standard purity, and by extension anything genuine or excellent.

clue.text: Resisted and passed on snatching iron up!

indicators.note: snatching means the word for passed on grabs the iron inside it

parts.note: to pass on is to die

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the iron symbol is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone resisted and died while grabbing an iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the chemical symbol upwards in this down clue, and 'snatching' tucks it into the word for passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy someone is to resist or openly refuse to obey them.

clue.text: Student ran, celebrating, gaining admission

indicators.note: gaining means the run of words contains the answer, which they carry inside them

explanation.surface: A student runs about, delighted to have won a place at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is the right to enter a place, and entrance means the same.

clue.text: Rising number divided by radius for bottle

indicators.note: divided by means the radius letter splits the turned number
in a down clue rising means the number is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A climbing figure is divided by a circle's radius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads the number upwards in this down clue; 'divided by' splits it with R. 'Bottle' is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves of steel means courage, the same as bottle in British slang.

clue.text: Manservant left Queen following anyway

indicators.note: following means the left and Queen pieces come after the word for anyway

parts.note: but can mean anyway, as in 'but I digress'
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A servant has quit, though the Queen gets on with things regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household.

clue.text: Sausage could provoke British ire

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A poor sausage could make a Briton furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' is British slang for a sausage; 'could provoke' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is the everyday British word for a sausage, from its habit of bursting in the pan.

clue.text: Trouble, fiery occasionally, with sex in part

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of fiery is used
in means the word for sex goes inside the portion

parts.note: a ration is a portion or part
it is a coy word for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A fiery temper sometimes causes trouble in a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of fiery; 'it' is an old coy word for sex, which 'in' puts inside the portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritation is annoyance, the kind of trouble that bothers someone.

clue.text: White china plate's finish

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate, so a pal

indicators.note: finish means the last letter of plate's, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A white china plate with its glazed finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china plate' is Cockney rhyming slang for mate; here it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale means light in colour, close to white, as a face drained of colour.

clue.text: Streak showing skin

definitions.meaning: to rush along at speed, as one might streak
an animal's skin with its fur

explanation.surface: A streaker reveals bare skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelting along means running very fast, and a pelt is an animal hide.

clue.text: Worship about taking till doomsday

indicators.note: taking means the word for about holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: re means about, concerning
ever means for all time, until the end of the world

explanation.surface: Someone will worship until the end of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' makes the short word for about hold the phrase for all time.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to venerate or hold in deep respect, a synonym of worship.

clue.text: House landlord eventually providing copious water?

indicators.note: eventually means the last letter of landlord

parts.note: welling means rising up and pouring out, as water from a spring

explanation.surface: A landlord at last lets a house that gushes water everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a home, the place where someone lives.
